decisions.reason: The custom-engineered citrus harvesting crate required tooling and design investment for a specific agricultural niche, so dropping it would write off sunk molds, and its mention through 2019 suggests ongoing commitment.
The foldable large container had a dedicated page in both years, signalling visible public commitment and heavy tooling investment that management would persist with and justify.
Stackable crates are core to the reusable packaging range and their molds are a sunk investment, so management keeps the product and attributes weak results to temporary market conditions.
The rackable pallet fits the firm's central pallet business and announced sustainability direction, so withdrawing it would expose the launch decision and waste tooling.
Its downgrade from its own page to a mention signals waning public commitment in a niche, but the sunk tooling and the chance that results are temporary still favor keeping it.
Visibility also declined after 2018, yet the pallet variant shares the firm's pallet platform and sunk investment, so management keeps it rather than admit a mistake.
